correctness.rationale: The source normalized ODE was checked from its full PDF. At criticality, direct differentiation gives a nonpositive logarithmic Lyapunov identity; the Cauchy bound uses exactly the simplex constraint. The zero-infection invariant face is the only zero-derivative set, proving global convergence. The infected two-by-two Metzler matrix has one simple zero eigenvalue and one strictly negative eigenvalue. A stable spectral projection, using the relative slow variation of the positive infected weight, proves I/E tends to delta/(gamma+mu). Linear forced-response ratios then give recovered and both susceptible deviations relative to E. Finally (1/W)′ tends to \(K/H\)>0; all component limits and logarithmic incidence follow. A rational checker and late-time ODE simulation corroborate but do not prove the global theorem.

originality.rationale: Closed-threshold global disease-free stability is known in general differential-susceptibility epidemic theory, so it is not claimed independently. The accepted new assertion is the complete source-specific critical relaxation vector and the exact susceptibility-variance effect on its nonzero decay constant at fixed reproduction number. The primary 2024 source analyzes only strict subthreshold global stability. Closest general 2009 and 2023 full texts were read; their relevant results do not supply the present rate or feedback coefficient. Search absence alone is not asserted to prove originality.
residual_risks: Bonzi et al. 2011 full text was not materially readable through the attempted open-access endpoint; its published abstract does establish broader equality GAS.
A stronger universal critical asymptotic theorem may imply the formula after a nontrivial specialization and may have been missed by terminology-based searches.
The comparison concerns a deterministic critical model, not a general causal claim for real-world epidemic intervention or changing average transmission.

value.rationale: The critical reproduction boundary governs whether disease goes extinct while exhibiting long tails; the source only addresses strict \(\mathcal R_0<1\). The theorem gives a natural complete leading-order classification of every compartment and the accumulated infections at exact criticality. Its exact variance law resolves a nontrivial question invisible to R0: two parameter sets with identical reproduction number can exhibit systematically different critical relaxation and cumulative burden. The role of immunity loss, infection progression, and protection heterogeneity is explicit, not a generic textbook restatement.
